name: Rooted Down-Set Embedding
statement: A graph $G$ is a daisy cube when there are a root $u$, a finite coordinate set $X$, and an isometric embedding $\varphi\colon V(G)\to2^X$ such that $\varphi(u)=\varnothing$ and $\varphi(V(G))$ is a down-set under inclusion.
comments: Equivalently, the image is the union of the Boolean intervals from the empty set to its inclusion-maximal members.
